sections.title: Hosea's Marriage
sections.description: Hosea's marriage with Gomer as a picture of God's relationship to Israel

sections.title: The Charges Against Israel
sections.description: Israel's unfaithfulness and lack of knowledge of God

sections.title: Hope for Restoration
sections.description: Charges against Ephraim and the promise of final restoration

events.title: Hosea's Call and Marriage to Gomer
events.description: God commands Hosea to marry Gomer, an unfaithful woman, as a living parable of Israel's unfaithfulness toward God. Hosea obeys the Lord's word and takes Gomer as his wife. The marriage becomes a prophetic sign illustrating the relationship between God and His unfaithful people.

events.title: Children with Symbolic Names
events.description: Gomer bears three children whom God gives symbolic names: Jezreel (God sows), reminding of bloodguilt; Lo-Ruhama (not loved), because God will no longer show mercy to the house of Israel; and Lo-Ammi (not my people), because Israel has broken covenant with God.

events.title: The Promise of Restoration
events.description: Amidst judgment comes a promise of hope: Those who were called 'not my people' will again be called 'children of the living God.' The peoples of Israel and Judah will be gathered under one leader, and the day of Jezreel will be great. The names of the children are turned into blessings.

events.title: Accusation Against the Unfaithful Wife
events.description: God speaks through the image of an unfaithful wife who runs after her lovers and attributes to them the gifts she received from her husband. The Lord will block her paths and make her realize that things were better before. Israel has forgotten that it was God who gave grain, wine, and oil.

events.title: God's Faithful Love
events.description: God promises to win back his bride with tenderness. He will lead her into the wilderness and speak tenderly to her heart. In that day she will call him 'my husband.' God will betroth himself to her forever in righteousness, justice, goodness, and mercy.

events.title: Hosea Buys Gomer Back
events.description: God commands Hosea to love his wife again, even though she is unfaithful. Hosea buys her back for fifteen shekels of silver and a homer and a half of barley. In the same way, the people of Israel will live for a long time without king or prince, but eventually turn and seek the Lord their God.

events.title: Accusation Against Priests and People
events.description: The Lord brings a lawsuit against the inhabitants of the land, because there is no faithfulness, no love, and no knowledge of God in the land. The priests receive especially harsh criticism because they have rejected knowledge and forgotten God's law. The people perish for lack of knowledge.

events.title: Israel's False Repentance
events.description: The people say: 'Come, let us return to the Lord! He who tore us will heal us.' But God sees through their superficial repentance. Their loyalty is like morning mist, like dew that disappears early in the day. God declares: 'I desire love, not sacrifice; knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.'

events.title: God's Love for Israel
events.description: God remembers with tenderness how he loved Israel as a child and called his son out of Egypt. He taught Ephraim to walk and took them up in his arms. But the people turned away. God's heart is moved within him, and his compassion awakens. He will not carry out his burning anger, for he is God and not a human.

events.title: Accusation Against Ephraim
events.description: Ephraim chases after the wind and runs after the east wind. They make a pact with Assyria and send oil to Egypt. The Lord reminds them of Jacob, who struggled with God, and calls the people to repentance. But Ephraim has become guilty of bitter sin and has provoked their Lord.

events.title: The Call to Repentance and the Promise of Healing
events.description: The prophet concludes with a heartfelt call for Israel to return to the Lord. The people are urged to pray: "Forgive all guilt and accept what is good." God promises to heal their apostasy and love them freely. He will be like dew for Israel, and they shall blossom like a lily and take root like the trees of Lebanon.
